instrumentation.sensor_sensitivity.title: Sensor sensitivity (Δoutput / Δinput)

variables.name: S
variables.desc: sensitivity = output change per input change [output]/[input]

variables.name: dy
variables.desc: output span Δoutput (in the sensor output units)

variables.name: dx
variables.desc: input span Δinput (in the measurand units)

assumptions: Static sensitivity over the linear range: S = (y_max − y_min)/(x_max − x_min). Enter Δoutput and Δinput in the sensor’s own units; S carries [output]/[input].
method_references: S = Δoutput/Δinput (slope of the calibration curve)

instrumentation.sensor_span.title: Sensor range and span
assumptions: The measurement range is the interval [x_min, x_max]; its width is the span.
method_references: Span = upper range limit − lower range limit

instrumentation.adc_resolution.title: Quantisation resolution of an n-bit ADC

variables.name: res
variables.desc: resolution = one least-significant bit (LSB), in the input units

assumptions: Uniform quantisation: Q = FS/2ⁿ. Some texts use FS/(2ⁿ − 1) when full scale maps to the top code; the difference is negligible for n ≳ 8.
method_references: Quantisation step Q = FS/2ⁿ for a uniform n-bit converter

instrumentation.strain_gauge.title: Strain gauge factor (GF = (ΔR/R)/ε)
assumptions: Linear gauge response; typical metal-foil gauge factors are near 2 (user input). ε is the engineering strain along the gauge axis.

instrumentation.wheatstone_bridge.title: Wheatstone bridge output voltage (strain gauges)

variables.name: eps
variables.desc: strain magnitude at each active gauge
variables.label: ε

assumptions: Linearised bridge (ΔR/R ≪ 1). Active gauges must be arranged to add: adjacent arms of opposite sign (bending pair) or all four arms with the right signs. Quarter (k = 1), half (k = 2), full (k = 4) bridge.

instrumentation.thermocouple_seebeck.title: Thermocouple voltage (linear Seebeck approximation)

variables.name: V
variables.desc: thermocouple emf (negative when the junction is colder than the reference)

assumptions: Linear (constant-Seebeck) approximation, valid over a small temperature span. The Seebeck coefficient is a user input (a single value, not the NIST ITS-90 table).

instrumentation.thermocouple_polynomial.title: Thermocouple voltage (user polynomial coefficients)

variables.name: coeffs
variables.desc: polynomial coefficients [c0, c1, …] in V/K^i (V = Σ c_i (T−Tref)^i)

variables.name: V
variables.desc: thermocouple emf (negative when the junction is colder than the reference)

procedure.python:
def _thermocouple_poly(v):
    """Thermocouple emf from a user-supplied polynomial in the junction−reference temperature difference.

    V = Σ c_i (T_junction − T_ref)^i, with coefficients c_i in V/K^i (c0 in V, c1 in V/K, …). The
    coefficients are user inputs from a calibration or a published table (e.g. NIST ITS-90); none are built
    in because the standard coefficients are temperature-range specific and must not be recalled.
    """
    coeffs = v['coeffs']
    if not isinstance(coeffs, (list, tuple)) or not coeffs:
        raise MechError('coeffs: give coefficients [c0, c1, …] of V = Σ c_i (T−Tref)^i (V/K^i)')
    dT = v['T_junction'] - v['T_ref']
    volts = 0.0
    for i, c in enumerate(coeffs):
        volts += float(c) * dT ** i
    return {'V': volts}

assumptions: Coefficients are user inputs from a calibration or a published table (e.g. NIST ITS-90 sub-range polynomials, whose coefficients are temperature-range specific and are not built in here). V = Σ c_i (T_j − T_ref)^i.

instrumentation.rtd_cvd.title: RTD resistance (Callendar–Van Dusen)

variables.name: R0
variables.desc: resistance at 0 °C (e.g. 100 Ω for a Pt100)

variables.name: C
variables.desc: Callendar–Van Dusen coefficient C, used below 0 °C (IEC 60751 nominally -4.183e-12 1/K^4)

variables.name: T
variables.desc: absolute temperature (enter e.g. -50 degC or 223.15 K; converted internally to °C)
variables.label: T

procedure.python:
def _rtd_cvd(v):
    """Platinum RTD resistance by the Callendar–Van Dusen equation.

    T is an absolute temperature (K); it is converted internally to T_C = T − 273.15 (°C). Then
    R = R0 (1 + A·T_C + B·T_C² + C·(T_C − 100)·T_C³) for T_C < 0 °C and R = R0 (1 + A·T_C + B·T_C²) for
    T_C ≥ 0 °C. A, B, C are user inputs; IEC 60751 nominals (A = 3.9083e-3, B = −5.775e-7,
    C = −4.183e-12) are commonly quoted but not built in.
    """
    R0, A, B, C, T = v['R0'], v['A'], v['B'], v['C'], v['T']
    T_C = T - 273.15
    if T_C < 0.0:
        R = R0 * (1.0 + A * T_C + B * T_C ** 2 + C * (T_C - 100.0) * T_C ** 3)
    else:
        R = R0 * (1.0 + A * T_C + B * T_C ** 2)
    return {'R': R}

assumptions: Callendar–Van Dusen with T_C = T − 273.15 (°C): R = R0(1 + A·T_C + B·T_C²) for T_C ≥ 0 °C, and R = R0(1 + A·T_C + B·T_C² + C(T_C − 100)T_C³) for T_C < 0 °C. A, B, C are user inputs — the IEC 60751 nominal values are quoted in the descriptions only.
method_references: Callendar–Van Dusen equation for platinum RTDs

instrumentation.lvdt.title: LVDT output voltage (V_out = S·x)

variables.name: V_out
variables.desc: output voltage (about the null, sign follows displacement)

variables.name: S
variables.desc: LVDT sensitivity (volts per metre of core displacement)

assumptions: Linear region of the LVDT, displacement measured from the null (zero) position.

instrumentation.accelerometer.title: Accelerometer output voltage (V_out = S·a)
assumptions: Charge/voltage sensitivity is the ratio of output to applied acceleration; the relation is linear within the sensor bandwidth.

instrumentation.snr.title: Signal-to-noise ratio (power) and decibels

variables.name: SNR_dB
variables.desc: signal-to-noise ratio in dB (negative when the signal is below the noise)

assumptions: Power ratio: SNR_dB = 10 log10(P_sig/P_noise). For amplitude (voltage) ratios use 20 log10 (see the decibel calculator).

instrumentation.decibel.title: Decibels from a voltage (amplitude) ratio
assumptions: Amplitude ratio: dB = 20 log10(V2/V1). For power ratios use 10 log10 (see the SNR calculator).

instrumentation.nyquist.title: Nyquist frequency from the sampling rate
assumptions: To represent a signal without aliasing the highest signal frequency must be below f_s/2 (Nyquist–Shannon).

instrumentation.aliased_frequency.title: Aliased (folded) frequency of an undersampled signal

variables.name: f_alias
variables.desc: apparent (aliased) frequency in the sampled record

assumptions: Closed form f_alias = |f_sig − f_s·round(f_sig/f_s)|. The mapping is many-to-one (folding), so the true frequency is not recoverable from the alias alone.

instrumentation.uncertainty_propagation.title: Uncertainty propagation (sympy partial derivatives)
assumptions: First-order (linearised) propagation for uncorrelated inputs: u_y = sqrt(Σ (∂f/∂x_i · u_i)²). Values and uncertainties are plain numbers in consistent units.
method_references: Law of propagation of uncertainty (GUM, uncorrelated case)

instrumentation.standard_error.title: Standard error of the mean (SE = σ/√n)

variables.name: sigma
variables.desc: sample standard deviation (in the data units)
variables.label: σ

assumptions: For n independent measurements of the same quantity; the standard error of the mean shrinks as 1/√n.

instrumentation.first_order_response.title: First-order sensor step response and time constant

variables.name: y
variables.desc: output at time t (in the output units)

variables.name: frac
variables.desc: fraction of the final value reached, y/y_ss

assumptions: First-order (single-lag) system: at t = τ the output reaches 1 − e⁻¹ ≈ 63.2 % of the final value. The output y carries the same units as y_ss.

instrumentation.second_order_params.title: Second-order sensor natural frequency and damping ratio (m, c, k)

variables.name: zeta
variables.desc: damping ratio (ζ < 1 underdamped, ζ = 1 critical, ζ > 1 overdamped)
variables.label: ζ

assumptions: Single-degree-of-freedom mass–spring–damper model of a seismic sensor (accelerometer, geophone). ζ < 1 underdamped (the usual design); ζ = 1 critically damped; ζ > 1 overdamped.

instrumentation.second_order_freq_respon.title: Second-order sensor frequency response (amplitude ratio and phase)

variables.name: phase
variables.desc: phase lag of the output relative to the input (−atan2(2ζr, 1−r²))

assumptions: Steady-state sinusoidal response of a second-order sensor; r = ω/ωn is the excitation frequency normalised by the undamped natural frequency. At resonance r = 1 the amplitude ratio is 1/(2ζ) and the phase is −90°.
